content: A prodrome refers to an early phase of a disease characterized by non-specific symptoms that precede the appearance of more specific clinical manifestations. These early symptoms serve as a warning sign of an impending illness. For instance, symptoms such as fever, general discomfort (malaise), headache, and loss of appetite (anorexia) are commonly observed during the prodromal phase of mumps or various infectious diseases. In the context of chronic neurological disorders, a prodrome can act as a precursor to conditions such as migraines or epilepsy. Symptoms during this phase may include visual disturbances like scotoma (partial loss of vision or a blind spot), confusion or disorientation, difficulty with speech (aphasia), or heightened sensitivity to light (photosensitivity). The term prodrome is also used to describe the initial phase of viral replication within a living organism (in vivo). Additionally, in obstetrics, prodromal labor—often referred to as false labor—represents the early signs and symptoms that occur before the onset of true labor. This phenomenon is sometimes associated with Braxton Hicks contractions.
